title: 169 · Claude kinetic type, morph, grid, particle and generative reel

scenes.name: White center point pulses
Fine concentric ring grows
Red scan line and two rings expand with HUD
Orange band opens vertically and CLAUDE rises
CLAUDE title subtitle and blue underline
SHAPE overscale entrance and color flash
SHAPE on blue outline typography rows
SHAPE thin horizontal exit slit
TIME on orange outline typography rows
TIME thin horizontal exit slit
RHYTHM on dark outline typography rows
RHYTHM staggered compressed strip exit
FEEL on lavender outline typography rows
FEEL slides away and leaves red point
Circle morphs to rotating square
Square morphs to triangle
Triangle morphs to star
Star morphs to hexagon
Nested grid tiles pop and expand radially
Sixteen-column quarter-circle grid turns in waves
Six thousand particles converge into digits
Particle digits 2026 shimmer and hold
Digits burst into radial white and orange streaks
Pale flash reveals recursive square tunnel
Rotating depth tunnel rings and speed streaks
Yellow staggered bars cover depth tunnel
Two-frequency damped harmonograph and serif text
Stepped orange blue lavender color transition
Final CLAUDE masked letters rise
Red dot and motion designer subtitle appear
Feature names reveal in sequence
HUD disappears and final title holds
Title shrinks into center with authored trails
Red dot closes full film

Kinetic scale, per-letter masks, outline row scrolling, echo/slit compression and cut timing are authored from observed chronology.
Shape morph uses angle-sampled polygons and closed-form elastic easing; the exact source vertex correspondence, rotation/trail phase and orbit positions differ.
Quarter-circle palette/map and rotation waves are code-authored from visible grid; some corner sectors, pivots and time phase differ.
6000 particles are sampled from independent font geometry; source digit contours, distribution, glitter, convergence and streak trajectories differ.
Recursive depth tunnel uses authored perspective rotation/speed, strokes/corner dots/trails; source depth camera and exact square phase differ.
Harmonograph uses observed frequency/damping labels as parameters with authored phase/scale; exact source curve phase and moving point are not recovered.
All 15 seconds are rebuilt; output30fps samples original60fps at half the source frame rate.
